title: Set, Clear and Toggle One Bit
statement: You are given a non-negative whole number n and a bit position p. Bit 0 is the lowest bit. Print three numbers on three lines. Line 1: n with bit p set to 1. Line 2: n with bit p cleared to 0. Line 3: n with bit p toggled (flipped). Treat n as a 32-bit unsigned number.
inputFormat: One line with two integers: n and p, separated by a space.
outputFormat: Three lines. The set result, the cleared result, and the toggled result. Each is a non-negative integer.
constraints: Results must stay within 32 bits (0 to 4294967295)
explanations: 5 is 101 in binary. Bit 1 is 0. Set gives 111 = 7. Clear leaves 5. Toggle flips it to 1, giving 7.
255 is 11111111 in binary. Bit 7 is already 1. Set gives 255. Clear gives 127. Toggle also gives 127.
reference:
import sys
n, p = map(int, sys.stdin.read().split())
m = 1 << p
full = 0xFFFFFFFF
print((n | m) & full)
print(n & ~m & full)
print((n ^ m) & full)
